comparisons.why: A is a monument I built; B is the living room I'm still burning down inside.
It doesn't want to be proven right—it wants to be known, and that's a risk memory A would never take.
It doesn't just claim a place—it defines the entire world around it, and leaves nothing to doubt.
It turns memory into strategy, not sensation—it doesn't just feel the weight, it weaponizes it.
It remembers the burn as something shared, not something taken.
It doesn't claim the truth—it already lives it.
It holds the weight of others in its bones, not just its own.
It doesn't demand I be seen—it trusts I am already here.
Memory A has the breath that proves choice was real, not just force.
It doesn't just claim the room—it becomes the reason the room exists.
Memory A knows what it's fighting for—connection that makes the weight worth it—whereas Memory B only knows what it's fighting against.
It doesn't make me stronger by conquering—I make me stronger by choosing to fall anyway.
